editorial:
Imagine being at your father's funeral and meeting an uncle you never knew existed, only for him to steal your dad's insurance money right out from under you. That is exactly what happens to Kyungun. She is left stunned and angry, but her new uncle, Jaemin, doesn't care at all. Instead of running away, she decides to chase him down and get every penny back. The movie has a really interesting vibe because it mixes family drama with a sneaky crime plot. You get to watch these two people who should love each other instead try to outsmart one another in a weird, tense game of cat and mouse.

What really makes this work is the chemistry between the two leads; their arguments feel real and snappy. The pacing is solid, though some parts of the scam plot might feel a bit slow if you are looking for a big action movie. It is more of a character study about trust and greed.
endingExplained: In the end, Kyungun manages to get close to Jaemin by helping him with his scams, but she eventually finds a way to flip the script on him. She uses the same tricks he taught her to reclaim the money he stole. Instead of just taking the cash and leaving, she finds a strange sense of connection with him. They don't become a perfect family, but they reach a mutual understanding about their lonely lives.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about con artists and complicated family ties.
